disclosure: General media-buying heuristic on frequency-based ad fatigue, not tied to a specific named study.

claims.text: A frequency of 3 or more weekly views per person is commonly treated as the ad fatigue threshold in paid social media buying.
Rising frequency tends to correlate with falling CTR and rising cost per lead.
Refreshing the opening seconds of a video or swapping the lead image can reset ad delivery without rebuilding the campaign.
Frequency is a real, checkable column in Meta Ads Manager under Performance.
83% of happy customers say they'd refer a business, but only 29% ever do
claims.source: Widely cited referral marketing research (commonly attributed to Texas Tech University studies on word-of-mouth behavior)

claims.text: The Black Arrow platform tracks every referral, so you know who sent who

claims.claim: A 14/21/30-day win-back sequence can revive quoted-but-not-booked leads without ad spend.
claims.note: Presented as an illustrative example workflow, explicitly labeled as not a specific client's results.

claims.claim: The Day 30 breakup message often earns the most replies.
claims.note: Reframed from an absolute claim to a qualified general pattern ("often"), consistent with well-documented breakup-email behavior in sales copywriting, not a fabricated metric.
